content: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
author: Marcus Aurelius
story:
It is endlessly seductive to debate ethics, read books on self-improvement, and theorize about how an ideal person ought to live. It gives us the comfortable illusion of progress while saving us from the real risk of action. Marcus, running an empire through plague and warfare, had zero patience for philosophical posturing.

Virtue is not a theoretical debate or an identity you wear for others. It is the immediate, unglamorous choice to be honest, courageous, and fair in whatever situation sits in front of you right now.
reflectionPrompt: Where in your work or relationships are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action right in front of you?

originalQuote: Waste no more time arguing over what a good man should be. As if the thing itself were not more clearly defined by this: 'Be one.'
